hypotheses.construction_plan: Start with the shared-kernel template K(n)*theta and specialize theta to a(n) or b(n) to recover the two product terms. The common factor K(n) remains fixed.
required_assumptions: K, a, and b are defined for the same symbol n
multiplication is associative enough to place theta immediately after K(n) in the template
hypotheses.rationale: The two product terms are non-identical only in the second factor and share the same multiplicative kernel K(n); MatchPy/LGG observations report an AC Mul pattern and a frozen LGG template theta0*K(n) with one hole, matching this one-parameter specialization.
